messages:
jo: Heads-up — hit a parity bug in the Next + LangChain sample where LangChain 'callbacks' (tool invocation events) look different between the JS and Python SDKs. The sample's eval harness expects a tool_start/tool_end sequence but Py emits tool_start then a final 'generation' event.
liam: ouch. Which sample and which SDK versions?
jo: devex-starters/langchain-playground, notebook uses redwood-py 0.8.2, the JS example used @redwood/sdk-js 0.8.0. Repro: run the eval harness that records callback events while calling an agent with a tool that streams. The harness asserts the sequence [tool_start, tool_stream, tool_end]. On Python I get [tool_start, tool_stream, generation_end].
anya: can you paste the minimal harness snippet and a chunk of the captured events?
jo: snippet: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor
client = RedwoodClient(os.environ.get("REDWOOD_DEV_TOKEN"))
agent = AgentExecutor.from_agent_and_tools(..., client=client)
rec = run_and_record_callbacks(agent, input_text)
assert rec.events == expected_sequence
```
captured events (sanitized):
```
[{
  "t": "tool_start",
  "tool": "wiki_search"
},
{
  "t": "tool_stream",
  "chunk": "The page says..."
},
{
  "t": "generation_end",
  "meta": {}
}]
```
expectation was a final `tool_end` event so the harness correlator knows to close the tool span.
liam: that will break a lot of our LangChain-based evals. JS shows tool_end as expected?
jo: yes JS emits tool_end. I tracked it to SDK-level framing of streaming tool outputs vs model generation finalization. JS treats streamed chunks from tools and then emits tool_end. Python's SDK maps stream termination to generation_end which LangChain treats as model-level signal.
anya: SDK parity issue then. Quick mitigation: relax the harness to accept both terminal events and normalize generation_end -> tool_end when the current active span is a tool. But long-term SDK should emit tool_end for tool streams to match JS and LangChain expectations.
liam: agreed. Also we should add an integration test in devex-starters that runs the full LangChain agent with a mock tool that streams and asserts the canonical sequence, so future changes don't break agents.
jo: I opened PR against devex-starters with the harness fix (accept both) and added a normalization layer in the sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-starters/pull/990
sdk-team: ISSUE-990 created to track emitting tool_end in python-sdk for streamed tools. Assigned to @liam. Proposed change: when a streaming tool completes, emit a `tool_end` event before `generation_end`. Add config flag `sdk.emit_tool_end_for_streams` default true for parity.
anya: can we also add a quick smoke test in eng-ml/evals that runs a live agent with a tiny mocked tool server that streams 5 chunks then closes. The eval should assert we see tool_start, multiple tool_streams, tool_end, generation_end in that order. I'll add it to nightly.
liam: PR for SDK work incoming. Plan: implement event ordering change, add unit tests in python-sdk to validate event sequence, and cut a patch release if green. Also update release notes: "LangChain callback parity: tool_end emitted for streaming tools".
jo: thanks — merged the devex-starters change to tolerate both and added a note in the sample README about callback parity until SDK patch ships.
preview-bot: preview deploy for pr-990: https://preview.redwood.dev/devex-starters/pr-990 ready :rocket:
anya: follow-ups: 1) SDK owners to land parity change and patch-release, 2) eng-ml to add the mock-tool streaming eval to nightly, 3) update sample README and workshop slides so folks don't be confused by callback differences.
liam: will do. Assigning myself to ISSUE-990 and will ping when the patch is published.
jo: validated patched harness locally against mocked server — now works and the events normalized. Happy to close this thread once SDK patch is out. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
